 Actinogen receives $10.8 million R&D tax rebate as Xanamem results approach Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock Actinogen Medical Ltd ( ASX:ACW , OTC:ATGGF ) has received a $10.8 million research and development tax incentive rebate from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) for the 2026 financial year, strengthening its cash position ahead of pivotal Xanamem Alzheimer's disease trial results expected in mid-November. 
 The rebate, which includes interest, totalled $10,838,793. 
 Actinogen used part of the proceeds to repay $4.3 million in borrowings from Endpoints Capital, which had been advanced against the company's FY26 research and development tax incentive rebate. 
 After repaying the loan and associated interest, Actinogen received net proceeds of $5.99 million. 
 Cash position rises to $21.9 million 
 The rebate lifts Actinogen's pro-forma quarter-end cash position to $21.9 million when combined with its previously reported cash balance of about $15.9 million at September 30, 2026. 
 The company is now debt-free. 
 Australia's research and development tax incentive provides eligible companies with cash rebates through refundable tax offsets for qualifying research and development expenditure. 
 For Actinogen, the program remains an important source of funding as it advances the clinical development of Xanamem. 
 Xanamem results due in mid-November 
 Actinogen is approaching topline final results from its pivotal Phase 2b/3 trial of Xanamem in Alzheimer's disease, which are expected in mid-November. 
 The upcoming data represent a key clinical milestone for the company and its development program.
